decides: which Tersoff->BTE-DFT calibration governs the Ge-rich side at 1100 K (symbolic transfer law argmin x=0.645 vs interpolated calibration argmin x=0.43)

decision_rule.D1_winner: the calibration with smaller |ln(k_obs/k_pred)| at 1100 K wins; if both are within 10% of k_obs, or their |ln| errors differ by < 0.03, the verdict is 'undecided at this resolution'
decision_rule.D2_refit: append all in-domain x=0.7 nodes to the BTE node set, rerun transfer_law.py (same basis, same selection rule, no other change) and report the new 1100 K argmin x and 5% window
decision_rule.D3_screening_verdict: if the refit 1100 K argmin lies within 0.05 of one calibration's pre-acquisition argmin (0.645 symbolic, 0.43 interpolated), that answer is confirmed; otherwise both are refuted and the new argmin is reported with the window
decision_rule.D4_ledger: the outcome is ledgered as a shard operation: 'strengthen' on the winning calibration, 'downweight' on the loser (never forget; both remain archived)
decision_rule.sanity_gate: reject and rerun (logged deviation) only if k_obs(1100) lies outside the bracket of the neighbouring BTE nodes' physical range (x=0.5 and x=0.85 values at 700-1100 K, times 0.5 to 2)

runs.method: VCA + mass disorder, full iterative BTE
runs.protocol: party4_bte/run_bte_point.sh unchanged (same as the 18 party-4a points)

why_this_point: transfer_law/README.md: no BTE node above x=0.5 inside the domain at 1100 K; largest calibration disagreement per unit cost (about one guest CPU-hour)
